statement: The n=3 member of the degree-2n−3 family is the unrestricted cubic-surface line problem; its monodromy is W(E6) of order 51,840 in the action on 27 lines.

answer.text: The n=3 member of the degree-2n−3 family is the unrestricted cubic-surface line problem; its monodromy is W(E6) of order 51,840 in the action on 27 lines.

source.version: arXiv:2509.06785v1 (8 September 2025); full text previously checked in the catalogue and re-used here

scope: The n=3, d=3 member: all smooth cubic surfaces in P3, with no symmetry restriction.
notes: This supplies the cubic exception. The n=2 member is a line in P2 with D2=1, so its permutation action is trivially the identity; this last elementary case is a direct consequence of the already catalogued degree formula, not a separately attributed group theorem.
